motivating_finding.method: Full-population (2025-01-02..2026-07-27, 390 RTH days) joint-blocker-set replay: for every bull qualifying candidate (score>=8, level-tied trigger, valid level) whose FULL filter-layer blocker set equals {filter_8} EXACTLY (i.e., filter_8 is the ONLY reason this candidate failed evaluate_bullish_setup -- every other one of the 8 bull filters independently passed), the candidate was priced via the SAME real-OPRA + real exit_manager pipeline (backtest/lib/exit_manager_walk.walk_exit_manager, structure-stop enabled, RIBBON_RIDE exit shape, entry+1-at-OPEN, min 3 contracts, ATM strike) every trusted study in this repo uses.
motivating_finding.result: n=183 sole-blocked candidates across 78 distinct trading days; 177 priced (6 BS-synthetic-excluded, disclosed not blended); total +$8,738.00; per-trade +$49.37; win rate 36.7%; per-DAY-that-fires +$112.03 (total / 78 distinct days, the right denominator for a frequency question). Survives Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.10 across the 12 sole-blocker cohorts tested this session (one of only 3 that do, alongside bear:filter_8 [negative] and quality_lock [negative] -- both of which REINFORCE existing doctrine rather than proposing a change).
motivating_finding.days_would_be_net_new: 69 of the 78 days (88.5%) currently have ZERO entries at all -- this is not cannibalizing an existing trading day, it is filling an empty one. Only 9 of 78 already had a same-day entry from elsewhere in the book (would become a 2nd position, subject to the existing one-position-at-a-time constraint -- see caveats).
motivating_finding.oracle_caveat: ORACLE, HINDSIGHT, NOT ACHIEVABLE AS STATED -- every candidate priced independently, no one-position-at-a-time sequencing applied (matching day_report_card.py's own oracle-walk convention exactly). A live gate cannot see 177 independent outcomes in advance; this number is the UPPER BOUND the gate is currently leaving on the table conditional on filter_8 alone, not a forecast.

filter_8_bull_definition_as_read.rule: vd = vix_direction(vix_now, vix_prior); vix_pass = vix_now < 17.20 (VIX_BULL_LOW_THRESHOLD) or vd == 'falling'; if not vix_pass: blockers.append(8).
filter_8_bull_definition_as_read.hard_block_today: UNCONDITIONAL. evaluate_bullish_setup's signature has NO vix_soft_mode parameter at all (confirmed by reading the full signature, filters.py:1109-1128) -- unlike bear's filter 8, which already has a working vix_soft_mode escape valve (-1 score demerit instead of a hard block), bull has ZERO soft-mode path today. This asymmetry is exactly what this prereg proposes to close.
filter_8_bull_definition_as_read.what_the_sole_blocker_cohort_is: bull reclaim setups where VIX was NOT below 17.20 AND NOT falling -- i.e. VIX elevated-or-rising, but still under bull filter 9's separate HARD cap of 22.0 (a candidate blocked by BOTH filter_8 and filter_9 would show up in the 2+ overlap buckets, not this sole-blocker cohort). This is a moderately-elevated-VIX band, not a panic regime.

hypothesis: H1: bull-side filter 8 (VIX-low-or-falling requirement) is, like its already-suspect bear-side counterpart, a lagging/miscalibrated veto for the specific sole-blocker population, and adding a bull-side soft-mode (demerit instead of hard block) recovers a materially positive, still-significant slice of that population once walked at REAL entry timing (not the oracle's independent-candidate convention) and gated by the SAME 5-gate discipline the sibling filter_8 prereg uses. H0 (null): the oracle bound does not survive contact with real sequential entry (one-position-at-a-time, quality-lock, the OTHER 14 named gates now also exposed to bull candidates that used to be filtered out earlier), or fails the recent-window / drop-best / runner-anchor gates the way most single-gate relaxations in this codebase have (WEEKEND-TWELVE: 11 of 12 weekend lanes NULLed; filter 5 NULL, shadow signals NULL, shelf-hold-reclaim NULL).
